text:
maria: Ran a set of portability benches comparing 'flashlight' (our in-house FlashAttention variant) vs fused-triton + fallback-cuda on SM80 (A100) and SM90 (H100). Short summary: behavior diverges at seq>=1024 and with cold KV.

maria: Command I used for reproducibility:
```bash
./bench_attention --model=56B --kernel=flashlight --seq=1024 --batch=8 --cache=prefix --cuda=13.1 --reps=20
```

maria: Results (median p50 latency / toks/sec):
- SM80, flashlight: 210ms / 58kt/s
- SM80, fused-triton: 225ms / 54kt/s
- SM90, flashlight: 190ms / 65kt/s
- SM90, fused-triton: 176ms / 70kt/s  <-- here triton wins for long seq on SM90

arjun: Interesting — do we see kernel uplifts tied to CUDA version? which driver/cu?

maria: SM90 tests were on CUDA 13.1 + driver 535.x. SM80 was CUDA 12.2 + driver 525.x (internal nightly infra setup). I also tried SM90 on CUDA 12.2 and flashed worse perf + occasional fallback to scalar KV path.

olga: Any evidence the KV cache layout/alignments differ across arch and that's triggering slower memcopy or L2 thrash?

maria: Yes. nvprof traces show extra L2 read/write spikes when seq>1024 on SM90 flashlight path. Flamegraph attached in the run artifacts (see perf-bucket). Hypothesis: our shared-smem tile sizing is suboptimal for SM90's increased L2 concurrency, causing bank contention and fallback in the paging path.

sam: Could be also related to our batching heuristic. We switch to fused-triton when batch_size*seq > threshold (current threshold 15000 tokens). On SM90 the optimal threshold looks higher (around 25000) because kernel launch latency is relatively cheaper there. So we're switching too early to triton on SM90 for some workloads, causing regressions.

maria: I ran a small sweep of the heuristic at seq=1024:
- threshold 15k -> choose triton on SM90, throughput 70kt/s
- threshold 25k -> choose flashlight on SM90, throughput 66kt/s but 10% better p99 latency
- threshold 30k -> choose flashlight less often, memory footprint larger -> OOM on some configs

arjun: So it's a cost/latency tradeoff. We should make heuristic arch-aware (SM80 vs SM90) and cuda-version-aware. Also detect cold vs warm KV: warm KV tends to favor flashlight because of prefix reuse.

olga: For KV warmup behavior I saw the first 3 tokens have 3-4x higher latency on flashlight on SM90 due to stream sync in the current paged path. We can amortize by prefetching first N KV pages asynchronously.

perf-bot: Perf run 2134567890 completed. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/2134567890/ (logs, flamegraphs, nvprof, bench.json) :white_check_mark:

sam: Action items:
1) Maria + Arjun: open RT-4789 to add arch/cuda-aware heuristic and safe upper bound for threshold.
2) Olga: prototype async KV prefetch for first two pages, measure p50/p99 delta.
3) Maria: re-run SM90 tests on CUDA 12.2 and 13.4 to map kernel performance surface.
4) If we see consistent wins for triton on SM90 at long seq, add a runtime override 'kernel_preference=triton' per model/route.

maria: I'll sketch the heuristic change and push a small canary. Will also add telemetry tag when we choose fallback so we can count real traffic impact.

arjun: small note: watch for deterministic rounding differences between triton kernels and cuda kernels — eval suite caught micro-ML score diffs last time. Add regression flag in bench harness.

olga: I'll pair with maria on the prefetch patch tomorrow.

sam: Nice work. TL;DR: SM90 generally faster but kernel choice and KV warming + batching heuristic matter. Need arch-aware heuristic + async prefetch to avoid p99 regressions. :rocket:
